evidence: src/infrastructure/in-memory.ts: InMemoryProductRepository, InMemoryOrderRepository, SystemClock and UuidGenerator implement the domain ports ProductRepository, OrderRepository, Clock and IdGenerator.
src/infrastructure/seed.ts: seedCatalogue(products: ProductRepository) saves through the port abstraction, not a concrete store.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: the composition root builds the OrderService and InventoryService from the in-memory adapters and passes them to createApp(AppServices).
src/infrastructure/http.ts: createApp delegates all business behaviour to services.orders and services.inventory; toErrorResponse maps domain errors to HTTP statuses in one place.

src/infrastructure/http.ts: the state check is repeated in the POST /orders/:id/transitions handler and in parseStateQuery, but both delegate to the domain's isOrderState/ORDER_STATES, so the invariant is not duplicated.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The four files share one concern: concrete adapters and wiring for the application. http.ts is the Express adapter that maps HTTP requests to application services and domain errors to status codes. in-memory.ts implements the domain ports (ProductRepository, OrderRepository, Clock, IdGenerator). seed.ts fills the catalogue through the ProductRepository port. server.ts wires everything together. Each file goes through the module's own abstractions: server.ts builds the services from the in-memory adapters and passes them to createApp through AppServices, and seed.ts writes through the port instead of a concrete Map. Invariants stay in one place. Order-state membership is delegated to the domain's isOrderState/ORDER_STATES rather than copied, and business rules such as stock checks and transitions stay in the services and domain. There are two minor issues. First, http.ts builds the same 'state must be one of' validation twice: inline in the POST /orders/:id/transitions handler and again in parseStateQuery. Both delegate to isOrderState, so the rule itself is not duplicated. Second, SystemClock and UuidGenerator sit in a file named in-memory.ts even though they are not in-memory storage. That is a naming quirk, not a split into unrelated concerns. Neither issue reaches the Fail threshold.
